All are equal: the margin depends only on the population size.
n = 300 (margin 0.055): larger samples give less variable sample proportions.
n = 50 (margin 0.128): smaller samples are easier to measure exactly.

questions.prompt: Why must a sample be random for its margin of error to be meaningful?
questions.prompt_markup: Why must a sample be random for its margin of error to be meaningful?

choices.text: A random sample always has a margin of error of 0, so any error is bias.
A biased sample has a smaller margin of error than a random one.
The margin describes chance variation in random samples; a biased sample can be off by more.
The margin depends only on the size of the population, not the sample.

questions.correct_answer: The margin describes chance variation in random samples; a biased sample can be off by more.
questions.grading_note: The margin does not measure bias. The others are false: random samples have a positive margin, bias is not measured by the margin, and the margin depends on the sample size.

sections.skill: Evaluate reports that use margins of error

branch.new_demand: Use the margin of error to evaluate claims made in reports.
branch.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: planned margins of error are used to judge whether reported differences are meaningful.

questions.prompt: A poll shows candidate A at 51% and B at 49%, each with a margin of error of ±4 percentage points. A headline says "A leads." Evaluate.
questions.prompt_markup: A poll shows candidate A at 51% and B at 49%, each with a margin of error of ±4 percentage points. A headline says "A leads." Evaluate.

choices.text: Justified: the margin of error is the same for both, so it cancels and A leads by 2.
Not justified: A must have less than 50% support, since 51% - 4% is below 50%.
Justified: 51% is greater than 49%, and the poll used a large sample.
Not justified: the intervals 47%-55% and 45%-53% overlap, so either could lead.

questions.correct_answer: Not justified: the intervals 47%-55% and 45%-53% overlap, so either could lead.
questions.grading_note: The difference is within the margin of error.
